summary: Yes, model family meaningfully affects predictive performance on Adult income prediction. Among 4 diverse model families (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting), ROC-AUC ranges from 0.7498 to 0.9129 (19.1% difference). This difference persists consistently across repeated train/test splits.
methodological_choices: Preprocessing: missing values replaced with column mode, categorical features label-encoded, numerical features standardized via StandardScaler. Train/test split: 80/20 stratified by target class. Primary metric: ROC-AUC (appropriate for imbalanced binary classification). Model families compared: Logistic Regression (parametric), Decision Tree (rule-based), Random Forest (ensemble tree), Gradient Boosting (ensemble tree). 4 diverse families covering different learning paradigms.
verification_method: 10 repeated train/test splits with random seeds (42, 123, ..., 5555)
verification_result: Finding held stable across all repeats. ROC-AUC range in CV: 0.1630. Model ranking consistent between initial test set and repeated splits. Best performer across repeats: Gradient Boosting (mean ROC-AUC 0.9129). Worst performer: Decision Tree (mean ROC-AUC 0.7498). Conclusion: Model family choice SIGNIFICANTLY impacts performance.
